The root cause of the syntax error is that f-strings are not properly closed — specifically, the f-string spans multiple lines without being closed with a quote, which causes a SyntaxError.

This is a recurring issue due to improper string formatting in print statements. To fix it, each f-string must be closed with a matching quote and properly formatted.

I will now fix the code by ensuring all f-strings are properly closed and split long prints into multiple lines.

{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Check how many duplicate patient_ids there are
patient_id_counts = df['patient_id'].value_counts()
duplicate_patients = patient_id_counts[patient_id_counts > 1]

# Get the rows for duplicate patients
duplicate_rows = df[df['patient_id'].isin(duplicate_patients.index)]

# For each duplicate patient, check the sample_seq values
max_sample_seq_per_patient = duplicate_rows.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max()
min_sample_seq_per_patient = duplicate_rows.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].min()

# Check if all duplicates have sample_seq > 1
has_multiple_samples = (max_sample_seq_per_patient > min_sample_seq_per_patient)

# Print results in separate statements to avoid f-string issues
print('Number of patients with duplicate IDs:', len(duplicate_patients))
print('Patient IDs with duplicates (first 5):', duplicate_patients.index.tolist()[:5])
print('Max sample_seq per duplicate patient:')
print(max_sample_seq_per_patient)
print('Min sample_seq per duplicate patient:')
print(min_sample_seq_per_patient)
print('Are there patients with multiple sample_seq values?', has_multiple_samples.any())
print('Distribution of max sample_seq:')
print(max_sample_seq_per_patient.value_counts())"}
